summary: Iteration 12 (redesign + simulated purchase + memberships + catalog admin). Backend: 12/12 new pytest cases pass (quote math w/ and w/o use_credit, discounts only on kit base, shipping 0, idempotent checkout by request_id, timeline, admin status flow, cancel blocked after En camino, user cancel refunds Plus credits, favorite/repeat, Plus activate idempotent/cancel keeps credits, AI usage 429 after limit, admin memberships/profitability, one-time export links xlsx+csv, import preview w/ invalid SKU errors, public price/supplement unchanged). Extra probes found 1 HIGH bug: cycling Plus activate→cancel→activate grants a new $20 credit every time (3 cycles = $60) — monthly credit is not idempotent per user/month. Medium: admin can move orders backwards, producing an inconsistent timeline; concurrent duplicate checkout may return the '_placing' placeholder. Frontend (390x844): Home compact sections, catalog tier tags + 'Imagen ilustrativa' (38/38), kit → cart → checkout ($419 free; Plus $369.10 all / $389.10 none / $384.10 custom 5), address-incomplete toast, double-tap confirm → exactly 1 order, /order-confirmed 'Tu kit está confirmado', /order/[id] 5-step timeline + favorite toast, /plus → /plus-welcome ($20), /credits, Perfil plan card, /plan cancel sheet (credits kept $15), admin catalog export popup + import preview via file chooser (confirm disabled when errors), profitability toggle, memberships dashboard, settings plans confirm sheet, admin orders status change — all working. No deprecated Expo packages detected; no SafeAreaView issues detected.

critical.issue: Monthly Plus credit is keyed by plan 'since' (membership.py:33 key=f'plus:{user}:{since}:{i}'). Each re-activation has a new 'since', so activate→cancel→activate grants another $20 immediately. Reproduced: 3 cycles in a few seconds → wallet plus $60 (earned $60). Credits are kept on cancel, so this is unlimited free credit. Fix: key credits per user + calendar period (e.g. plus:{user}:{YYYY-MM} or track last_credit_period on user and only grant if a new 30-day period since last grant).

minor.issue: Backward transitions allowed (e.g. En preparación → Pedido confirmado returns 200). Timeline then keeps 'En preparación' done and 'Pedido confirmado' shows the newest timestamp (00:58) above 'En preparación' (00:57) because order_view builds reached={status:at} overwriting earlier entries (server.py:905). Either forbid moving backwards (only forward in ORDER_FLOW + Cancelado) or keep first timestamp. Admin UI also shows a 'Pedido confirmado' button for an order already in preparation.

3 parallel requests with the same request_id → 1 order (good) but one response returned the placeholder doc with status '_placing' and no items/total (business.py:375-379 returns prev while still placing). Also if place_order raises after inserting the placeholder, a '_placing' order remains forever and that request_id is burned. Suggest waiting/polling until status != '_placing' or returning 409 'procesando', and deleting the placeholder on failure.
use_ai() increments the monthly counter before the LLM call; if the LLM fails (503) the interaction is still consumed. Count only on success.

'Usuarios Plus' (17, from plan_view, excludes admins and moves Plus+institution users to institutional) vs 'Suscripciones activas' (26, raw count of plan.tier=plus & source=demo incl. any user) are inconsistent on the dashboard; also 'Créditos otorgados' is inflated by the activate/cancel exploit above.
Refund goes to the most recent credit benefit, not necessarily the benefit that was consumed (business.py:438). Low impact in demo.

ui_bugs.issue: After an admin backward status move, timeline timestamps appear out of order (Pedido confirmado 00:58 above En preparación 00:57). Root cause backend (see minor issue).

issues: Credit mode chips (checkout-credit-all/custom/none) are 40px tall (<44px touch target)
Validation toast overlaps the header; the page does not scroll to the first invalid field (fields below the fold), so users still have to find them
Empty 64px header bar with no title or back button at the top of /order-confirmed and /plus-welcome — looks like a blank strip

Quick-signal tile label 'Quiero estar a ...' is truncated (84px tiles, 2 lines)
Mi día card shows 'Hoy —' with 'Próxima actividad: Cita' (no time) — dash looks like missing data

action_items: HIGH: Make Plus monthly credit idempotent per user per period across re-activations (membership.py accrue_plus key / activate_plus). Reproduce with tests/probe_iter12_plus_cycle.py (expect $20, currently $60).
Forbid backward order status transitions in set_order_status (or keep first timestamp in order_view) and hide past-state buttons in admin/orders.tsx.
place_order: don't return the '_placing' placeholder to duplicate concurrent requests; clean up placeholder on exceptions.
Count AI usage only after a successful LLM response.
Align admin memberships counts (Usuarios Plus vs Suscripciones activas).
Minor UI: credit chips minHeight 44; Spanish labels in import preview; header strip on order-confirmed/plus-welcome; scroll to first invalid checkout field.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1364 lines and business.py 730 lines (>700) — consider splitting orders/cart into their own module.
checkout.tsx sends use_credit: b?.credit — if the quote is still reloading after changing the custom amount, the previous quote's credit is sent (minor race).
import_catalog confirm=true: top-level product cost fields come from the first variant only while unit_cost uses max over variants — fine but undocumented.
Import confirm=true was NOT executed against seeded products (would modify seed cost data); preview + price-unchanged checks done. Apply step needs a manual check.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run pytest with -n 0 to see prints (pytest.ini uses xdist). New users land on multi-step /onboarding ('Completar después' only advances one step). Order-confirmed page refetches /orders/{id}. Admin orders testIDs: admin-order-{number}-{status}.
rca_of_issue: Plus credit exploit: accrue_plus uses key plus:{user_id}:{plan.since}:{period_index}; activate_plus sets a fresh 'since' on every activation, so period 0 of each new subscription is a new unique key → new +$20 move. cancel_plus keeps the balance. Mitigation: derive the key from user + period start independent of subscription (or store last_credit_at on the user and only grant when >=30 days passed).
